records.reason: The mutated body belongs to the second send_abstract, which #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))] removes from every Linux build, so the mutant compiles to the very program the original does.
records.evidence: The item carries #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))] on the line above its signature, and rustc drops a cfg'd-out item before type checking, so on the only target this daemon builds for (a systemd unit, Type=notify, Linux) both the original and the mutant contain the other send_abstract, the one under #[cfg(target_os = "linux")], and the compiled code is identical: only the source-line numbers of the lines below the removed body differ, and no log line carries one. git grep -n 'send_abstract(' over the whole workspace finds five lines: three of Rust, all in crates/daemon/src/lifecycle.rs (the one call in send, line 152, and the two definitions, 157 and 164), and this record's own anchor and evidence; no other crate names it. The Linux definition's own mutant is killed by the abstract-socket case of the delivery test, which reads the datagram from an abstract socket.
